scope: Independent review of additional direct-audio methods after the 22 October tests; no product build, proxy, login, native code, browser security override or protected authentication workaround.

findings.hypothesis: MWEB ultralow/HLS availability for difficult tracks
findings.result: All three valid-song requests return UNPLAYABLE with refresh-page reason, including the independently playable control. No direct/HLS/DASH URL returned. This request variant is not a usable route; it is not evidence of absent songs or of every possible MWEB request.
All requests return device/client no longer supported, without usable formats. No CORS bypass/custom headers attempted.
Current primary client table documents that limitation, but these actual responses expose no Made-for-kids flag. Category is only a possible explanation, not established cause.

findings.hypothesis: SABR pure-JS parser avoids network limits
findings.result: Current Kira and the minimal GoogleVideo/Shaka example explicitly depend on an extension/proxy for browser requests. Their codec/parser support does not invalidate the earlier normal-origin SABR CORS failure; no unchanged SABR POST was replayed.

findings.hypothesis: Onesie uses a distinct public bootstrap
findings.result: Provider TV configuration responds HTTP200 but normal Pages and opaque origins both fail MissingAllowOriginHeader. Stopped before extracting client keys, encryption, trusted-proxy assertions, Onesie requests or media.

actualPlayback.proofScope: Desktop beginning-only progress; not full transfer, phone, background or screen-off proof

conclusion: No tested new direct method solves the difficult songs under the pure-PWA/no-account/no-proxy constraints. Keep these request variants and prerequisites as bounded negative evidence; prioritize other provider approaches rather than rebranding a native/proxied client as a PWA solution.
